data.gender_notes: Sudipti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the word 'sudipta', Sudipti signifies 'well-lit' or 'illuminated'. The name Sudipti carries the meaning “Well-lit” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sudipti usually hope their child will grow to embody well-lit and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Sudipti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Well-lit.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sudipti total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Sudipta was a king of the Vatsa kingdom in ancient India, located in the eastern part of the Indian subcontinent. He is known for his conquest of Magadha and his patronage of the Buddhist monk Mahavira. This occurred around the 6th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Vatsa kingdom, conquest of Magadha, patronage of Mahavira

historical_references.reference: Sudipta was a poet and close friend of the famous Sanskrit poet Kalidasa, who lived during the 4th and 5th centuries CE. In one of his works, Sukasastra, Suudipta is mentioned as a great poet and scholar, who composed poems on various topics including drama, poetry, and military strategy.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, friend of Kalidasa, poet and scholar
